# ListItem supplied-column frozen original phase

RQ-CF-PRG-LISTITEM-COLUMN-NUMERIC-001 /
VR-5611-LISTITEM-COLUMN-NUMERIC-001/002.

The helper remains unwired. This phase adds a separate safe-public test target
and four mode/session registrations for the exact-two-argument existing-ID
read. Each shard executes 92 independently expected reads across ListBox and
ComboBox, stable IDs 11/22, ordinary and metadata-sensitive Numeric operands,
bounded exact64 extensions, positive missing cells, default/exact-zero
RowSourceType, trim-empty ControlSource, localized error31, preserved state and
data-session/NumericBehavior isolation.

Unsafe nonfinite or out-of-int64 public coercions are excluded from original
execution; their helper containment remains direct-only until a separately
authored fixed-only hostile gate exists. The public expectations come from the
retained installed-VFP9 captures and named #5611/#6776 extension parents, not
the helper or the current caller.

GNU 15.2 and Clang 21.1 both compile the new target. CTest enumerates the direct
test, public target and four shards (six total), all with complete isolation
metadata. The bare public target validates the frozen 11 Numeric and four
exact64 source tables without invoking the unwired caller; each of the four
mode/session shards remains the only public execution path. A development
COPPERFIN/session1 execution reaches all 92 cases and
fails only as expected against the still-unwired legacy caller; this is frozen
original failure evidence, not acceptance. Both complete compiler-wide
original suites, their full raw/counter/source-hash audit and caller wiring
remain future gates.

The exact original-before-wire suite is frozen as 106 unique CTest subjects:
100 prior controls plus the unused direct helper, bare inventory and four public
mode/session shards. `frozen-original-inputs.sha256` covers the runtime public
headers and PRG engine implementation, all PRG-engine test sources, CMake and
isolation registrations, and the original driver/auditors. The deliberately
broad source inventory prevents an unrelated PRG test or included runtime file
from changing between the two compiler executions without detection.

Both complete original106 executions finished before caller wiring. GNU and
Clang each passed all 100 prior controls, the direct helper and the bare frozen
inventory, and failed only the four expected public mode/session shards. Every
shard executed 92 reads; the full 448 selected assertion failures were identical
between compilers (`b2bac3860ac8d537a68548ec128071d4735fc8907311f07c2724b989846d0cdc`),
with no unrelated assertion or sanitizer diagnostic. GNU raw SHA-256 is
`541f0ede2013c0e431d95bf885ee62c2f3a6659f0af896d71331e1d955628bbd`;
Clang raw SHA-256 is
`fa4fc5619c85d29a241d09033d04054961d57cb4c2090d2b54a6722e4340e1d9`.
The complete audit returned true; these failures remain pre-fix evidence, not
acceptance of the unwired caller.
